result.summary: Read core-directives.md and docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md in full, then the diff (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts, apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,en,ru}.ts, apps/bot/src/index.ts) line by line against the design. DESIGN CONFORMANCE: listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin (registration.ts) matches design §2.1 exactly -- LEFT JOIN profiles, INNER JOIN users, WHERE admission='admitted' only, SELECT clause structurally never names profiles.phone/profiles.email, ORDER BY asc(lastName), asc(firstName), asc(id) (Postgres's own NULLS LAST giving §2.1's ordering rule for free), deriveCheckinDisplayName implements the exact 5-row fallback table. countCheckedIn matches §2.2 -- one fresh SELECT count(checked_in_at IS NOT NULL), no admission predicate added (correctly reasoned as redundant given the CHECK constraint, §2.2's own stated reasoning). decideCheckinToggleOutcome matches §3.1's 4-step first-match-wins table exactly, pure, no I/O. toggleCheckIn matches §3.2 exactly: db.transaction, SELECT...FOR UPDATE is the ONLY read of admission/checkedInAt inside this function -- confirmed the callback_data patterns (CHECKIN_TOGGLE_PATTERN = /^checkin:toggle:(.+)$/) carry only registrationId, no admission/eventId encoded anywhere, so there is structurally nothing stale for toggleCheckIn's own FOR UPDATE read to inherit; refusal branches (not-found/refused-not-admitted) write nothing and return before any UPDATE; check-in/undo branches write exactly one audit_log row each in the same transaction as the UPDATE (S8). checkin.ts's makeCheckInHandler steps 1-6 are unchanged from REQ-018's stub (confirmed by reading REQ-018's design and comparing); step 7 composes buildCheckinView correctly. Toggle callback handler re-authorizes via requireEventStaffForEvent (confirmed byte-identical import, no modification to eventStaffAuthorization.ts -- that file has zero diff against master) before calling toggleCheckIn -- matches §3.3/§4.2 exactly, including the deliberate no-message-edit-on-refusal behavior (§4.2 step 5, §6 OQ1). Page callback re-runs the same gate per §4.3. i18n additions match §5's catalog exactly (10 new/kept keys, authorizedStub correctly removed as dead). DOMAIN-VS-HANDLER PLACEMENT (decisions/0004) CONFIRMED CORRECT: listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin/countCheckedIn/decideCheckinToggleOutcome/toggleCheckIn all live in domain/registration.ts, which has zero grammY import (confirmed by reading the file's import list). checkin.ts's handlers call these functions and do no admission/write-eligibility decision themselves -- the toggle callback handler only orchestrates (re-auth, call toggleCheckIn, branch on outcome.kind for message shape), it never re-implements decideCheckinToggleOutcome's logic. NO now()/current_timestamp IN A TIME-DEPENDENT PREDICATE: toggleCheckIn/decideCheckinToggleOutcome take no clock read at all (admission/checkedInAt are not time-dependent predicates); the handler's own `new Date()` calls are passed in as explicit `at`/`evaluationTime` parameters to toggleCheckIn and requireEventStaffForEvent, matching decisions/0006's discipline. requireEventStaffForEvent itself is unchanged (zero diff). REUSE OF requireEventStaffForEvent CONFIRMED UNWEAKENED: `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts` is empty -- byte-for-byte identical to master. Called at /checkin entry, at every toggle, and at every page turn, exactly per design. RESOLVEACTINGUSER-CALLED-TWICE JUDGMENT: accept as implemented, not a design-correction case. The design's authResult.user.id reference at §4.2 step 4 was a genuine inaccuracy against the ACTUAL (unchanged, REQ-018) shape of requireEventStaffForEvent's CheckInAuthorizationResult, which carries no `user` field on its ok:true branch (verified by reading eventStaffAuthorization.ts in full). BACKEND-DEV's fix -- calling resolveActingUser(db, tgId) a second time -- is the correct call for two reasons: (1) modifying the already-reviewed, security-relevant requireEventStaffForEvent to bolt on a `user` field would be an unreviewed change to a passed gate, for a plumbing need only; (2) there is no race risk from the two separate unlocked reads, because the only field toggleCheckIn's caller uses from ActingUser is `.id` -- the user's own primary key, which cannot change between resolveActingUser's two invocations (a users.id row is never repointed to a different person). The two calls are functionally two identical, cheap SELECTs by tg_id with no possibility of divergent results within the same request. Correctly flagged per core-directives 'never resolve a conflict silently' -- BACKEND-DEV's MINOR issue entry names the design/implementation mismatch precisely rather than silently patching around it. Filing a docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md correction (updating §4.2 step 4's text) is a documentation nicety, not a rework blocker; leaving it as a MINOR note is proportionate. INDEPENDENT AC RE-VERIFICATION (own fixtures, own test file, calling the domain functions directly -- bypassing grammY dispatch entirely, NOT trusting checkin.db.test.ts's own assertions): wrote apps/bot/src/domain/_reviewer-scratch-req028.test.ts (deleted immediately after use, confirmed via git status --porcelain), 3 tests against a live scratch Postgres: - AC1: registered an admitted registrant, captured registrationId, issued a raw SQL UPDATE admission='withdrawn' entirely outside any application code, then called toggleCheckIn directly -- outcome.kind === 'refused-not-admitted', checked_in_at/checked_in_by remained null, zero checkin/checkin_undo audit rows. This exercises the exact write-time recheck property AC1 is about (a fresh FOR UPDATE read happening strictly after the interleaved external write), independently of BACKEND-DEV's own test's specific fixture/dispatch path. - AC3: seeded a registrant with a real phone (+70001112233) and email (hidden@example.com) on their profile, called listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin directly, JSON-serialized the entire result array and confirmed neither raw string appears anywhere in it. - AC4: confirmed countCheckedIn(0) before any write, a raw SQL UPDATE setting checked_in_at directly (bypassing toggleCheckIn) is reflected as countCheckedIn(1) on the very next call (proving no cache), then exercised toggleCheckIn's own undo branch and reconfirmed countCheckedIn(0) and that the events row is byte-for-byte unchanged (toEqual) across the whole sequence. All 3 passed. Read (did not re-derive with a separate fixture, given time budget) AC2/AC5/AC6's own checkin.db.test.ts assertions line by line -- AC2's exactly-one-audit-row-per-write assertions, AC5's admission='admitted'-only WHERE clause (SQL-layer filter, not post-fetch), and AC6's case-insensitive substring filter over the already-fetched array (SEARCH_RESULT_LIMIT=20 comfortably above the 10+1 fixture) all match the design and are asserted correctly in the existing test file; ran the full suite (see below) and these tests pass for real, not vacuously (fixtures use distinct/adversarial names -- 'Hidden Waitlisted'/'Hidden Withdrawn' for AC5, 10 same-last-name 'Guest0..9 Common' rows plus one 'Zharkyn Unique' for AC6 -- the kind of adversarial-naming construction that would catch a coincidentally-passing filter). COMMANDS RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT: scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1) was already running; `DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx drizzle-kit migrate` (apps/bot) -> migrations applied successfully, zero new migration files (independently confirms design §0's 'no schema change' claim). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces clean. `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite, no path filter) -> 26 files / 272 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count. **`npm run lint` (repo root) FAILS -- this is the reason for this FAIL verdict, contradicting BACKEND-DEV's handoff claim of 'npm run lint -> exit 0, apps/bot 0 problems':** ``` apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts 496:11 error 'admitted' is assigned a value but never used @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars ✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings) ``` apps/web's lint is clean (only the 2 pre-existing unrelated warnings). The failure is in AC5's own test ('REQ-028 AC5 -- only admission=\'admitted\' rows appear'): `const admitted = await seedAdmittedRegistrant(eventId, { firstName: \"Gulnaz\", lastName: \"Waitlist-Never\" });` -- the binding is never read anywhere in the test body (the assertions below check buttonTexts/text directly, never `admitted.*`). This is squarely in this run's diff (the file is new in this diff, `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` includes it), so it is this run's failure per core-directives' 'in the diff is not the same as caused by the diff' -- here it plainly IS caused by the diff, not merely proximate. Per 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures', this must be fixed at the source (remove the unused binding or use it), not silenced. SCOPE: diff touches exactly the design's own file list plus docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md and this run's handoffs -- no scope creep. No new npm workspace, no build-output relocation -- the Dockerfile-coverage trigger in this role's own instructions does not apply; no scratch Docker build required.

evidence.lint_gate: FAIL -- apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts:496:11, unused `admitted` binding in the AC5 test, @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars. Structurally in this run's diff (new file). Not pre-existing (git diff --name-only master...HEAD confirms the file did not exist on master).
evidence.resolveActingUser_twice_judgment: ACCEPT AS IMPLEMENTED. No race risk: both calls read only ActingUser.id (a users.id primary key, immutable per row) via two unlocked, independent SELECTs by the same tg_id within one request; modifying the already-gated requireEventStaffForEvent to add a `user` field would be an unreviewed change to a security-relevant module for a plumbing-only need. The design's §4.2 step 4 reference to authResult.user.id is a genuine minor design inaccuracy (that field never existed on CheckInAuthorizationResult, confirmed by reading eventStaffAuthorization.ts, which the design itself lists as reused-unchanged) -- correctly flagged, not silently routed around.

issues.description: `const admitted = await seedAdmittedRegistrant(eventId, { firstName: "Gulnaz", lastName: "Waitlist-Never" });` in the AC5 describe block is never read; @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars fails the repo-root `npm run lint`. This is a hard gate (core-directives.md 'Unblock-Everything' / 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures') and must be fixed at the source -- either drop the binding (`await seedAdmittedRegistrant(...)` with no assignment) or use it in an assertion. BACKEND-DEV's step-02 handoff reported 'npm run lint -> exit 0, apps/bot 0 problems', which does not match what running it now produces -- either the lint run reported was against a different tree state, or it was not actually run against the final committed diff.

BACKEND-DEV's resolution (a second resolveActingUser(db, tgId) call) is correct and carries no race risk (see resolveActingUser_twice_judgment above) -- this is filed as a documentation-accuracy note for docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md, not a rework blocker.
